result.title: Staged Continual Adaptation of Multimodal Foundation Models for Japanese Financial Documents
result.comment: 17 pages, 10 figures, 9 tables. Presented at the ICML 2026 Workshop "Continual Adaptation at Scale: Towards Sustainable AI". Code: https://github.com/AtsushiYanaigsawa768/Compass
result.summary: Staged post-training of multimodal foundation models chains vision-language alignment, reasoning distillation, and domain tuning, yet how each phase trades capabilities against the others remains under-characterised. Tracking an 8.4B-parameter model from an un-fine-tuned baseline through three training phases on Japanese financial documents (evaluated on five text-input benchmarks), we find the phases interact non-additively: math-only distillation overwrites the financial knowledge acquired earlier even as procedural math skill survives, and the domain phase repairs more than it installs. A skip-phase ablation is best for domain knowledge but forfeits numerical-reasoning gains, so per-phase contributions are not decomposable and the best checkpoint is task-dependent, with implications for checkpoint retention and scheduling rather than added stages.

AI.brief_summary: 追踪一个 8.4B 多模态模型在日文金融文档上依次经过对齐、推理蒸馏与领域微调三阶段的演化，发现各阶段效果非可加：数学蒸馏会覆盖先前获得的金融知识，跳过某阶段的消融领域知识最好但失去数值推理收益，最优 checkpoint 依赖任务。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不研究 latent 推理或视觉证据使用（评测为文本输入基准），但分阶段训练相互干扰、贡献不可分解与最优检查点依赖任务等结论，可供核查 LVR 多阶段轨迹训练的遗忘与调度线索。
